metadata.question: Does the plume from Whakaari/White Island, New Zealand travel in a southern direction on January 7, 2025?

data.raw_code: The question: "Does the plume from Whakaari/White Island, New Zealand travel in a southern direction on January 7, 2025?" I need to: 1. Find imagery for January 7, 2025 over Whakaari/White Island. 2. Detect the volcanic plume and determine its direction. 3. Answer whether it travels south. Approach: - Use Sentinel-2 for visible plume detection (RGB bands). - Use MODIS or VIIRS for thermal anomalies (hot spots) if needed. - For plume direction: calculate the centroid/extent of plume pixels relative to the vent location. - Compare latitude of plume extent vs vent latitude. Geometry: Whakaari/White Island is at approximately 37.52°S, 177.18°E. Date: January 7, 2025 (specific date). Challenges: 1. January 7, 2025 is in the future for current datasets. 2. Need to check if imagery exists for that date. 3. If no image, try widening date range or using different sensors. 4. Plume detection: high reflectance in visible bands, maybe use NDVI/SWIR difference. 5. Direction analysis: compare mean latitude of plume pixels to vent latitude. Data strategy: 1. Try Sentinel-2 first (high resolution, visible bands). 2. If no Sentinel-2, try Landsat 8/9. 3. If still no data, try MODIS (daily coverage). 4. For plume: mask clouds, water, land; look for bright reflective features. Processing: 1. Get image for date ±1 day. 2. Cloud mask. 3. Create plume mask: high reflectance in blue/green bands AND not vegetation/water. 4. Calculate plume centroid or mean position. 5. Compare to vent location: if plume centroid is south of vent → southern direction. Validation: - Check if image exists (C1). - Check if plume pixels exist after masking (C2). - Check if calculations produce valid results (C3). Output: - Print image counts, pixel counts. - Final answer tag. Note: January 7, 2025 is in the future. Current GEE data might only go up to 2023/2024. We'll need to handle the "no data" case. Let me structure the code: 1. Define geometry (point buffer around White Island). 2. Try multiple collections with fallbacks. 3. Check for image existence. 4. Process to detect plume. 5. Analyze direction. 6. Output answer. ```javascript const ee = require('@google/earthengine'); const privateKey = require('../auth_keys/test-project-473922-29f05d49bed7'); async function runAnalysis() { // 1. Geometry & Time Definitions const whiteIsland = ee.Geometry.Point([177.18, -37.52]); // Note: [lon, lat] const region = whiteIsland.buffer(20000); // 20km buffer for plume detection // Target date: January 7, 2025 (future date - may not have data) const targetDate = '2025-01-07'; const startDate = ee.Date(targetDate).advance(-1, 'day'); // ±1 day window const endDate = ee.Date(targetDate).advance(1, 'day'); // Function to mask clouds in Sentinel-2 function maskS2Clouds(image) { const qa = image.select('QA60'); const cloudBitMask = 1 << 10; const cirrusBitMask = 1 << 11; const mask = qa.bitwiseAnd(cloudBitMask).eq(0) .and(qa.bitwiseAnd(cirrusBitMask).eq(0)); return image.updateMask(mask); } // Function to detect plume (bright, reflective features in visible bands) function detectPlume(image) { // Use visible bands: blue (B2), green (B3), red (B4) const visible = image.select(['B2', 'B3', 'B4']); const brightness = visible.reduce(ee.Reducer.mean()).gt(0.25); // High reflectance threshold // Mask out water (NDWI > 0) and vegetation (NDVI > 0.3) const ndwi = image.normalizedDifference(['B3', 'B8']).rename('NDWI'); const ndvi = image.normalizedDifference(['B8', 'B4']).rename('NDVI'); const notWater = ndwi.lt(0.1); // Not water const notVeg = ndvi.lt(0.3); // Not vegetation // Plume mask: bright, not water, not vegetation return brightness.and(notWater).and(notVeg); } // 2. Data Acquisition & Check let img = null; let collectionName = ''; // Try Sentinel-2 first (10m resolution, good for visible plume) let s2Col = ee.ImageCollection('COPERNICUS/S2_SR_HARMONIZED') .filterBounds(region) .filterDate(startDate, endDate) .map(maskS2Clouds); let s2Size = s2Col.size().getInfo(); console.log(`Sentinel-2 images (${targetDate} ±1 day): ${s2Size}`); if (s2Size > 0) { img = s2Col.median().clip(region); collectionName = 'Sentinel-2'; } else { // Try Landsat 8 let ls8Col = ee.ImageCollection('LANDSAT/LC08/C02/T1_L2') .filterBounds(region) .filterDate(startDate, endDate); let ls8Size = ls8Col.size().getInfo(); console.log(`Landsat 8 images (${targetDate} ±1 day): ${ls8Size}`); if (ls8Size > 0) { // Simple cloud mask for Landsat using QA_PIXEL function maskL8Clouds(image) { const qa = image.select('QA_PIXEL'); const cloudMask = qa.bitwiseAnd(1 << 3).eq(0) // Cloud .and(qa.bitwiseAnd(1 << 4).eq(0)); // Cloud shadow return image.updateMask(cloudMask); } img = ls8Col.map(maskL8Clouds).median().clip(region); collectionName = 'Landsat 8'; } else { // Try MODIS (daily, but lower resolution) let modisCol = ee.ImageCollection('MODIS/061/MOD09GA') .filterBounds(region) .filterDate(startDate, endDate); let modisSize = modisCol.size().getInfo(); console.log(`MODIS images (${targetDate} ±1 day): ${modisSize}`); if (modisSize > 0) { img = modisCol.median().clip(region); collectionName = 'MODIS'; } else { console.log(`C1`); return; } } } console.log(`Using ${collectionName} image`); // 3. Processing - Detect plume and count pixels let plumeMask; if (collectionName === 'Sentinel-2') { plumeMask = detectPlume(img); } else if (collectionName === 'Landsat 8') { // For Landsat 8, adjust band names: SR_B2 (blue), SR_B3 (green), SR_B4 (red) // Create a simple brightness mask const visible = img.select(['SR_B2', 'SR_B3', 'SR_B4']); const brightness = visible.reduce(ee.Reducer.mean()).gt(0.25); plumeMask = brightness; } else if (collectionName === 'MODIS') { // MODIS: surface reflectance bands 1-7 const brightness = img.select('sur_refl_b01').gt(0.25); // Band 1 (red) plumeMask = brightness; } // Count plume pixels const plumeCount = plumeMask.reduceRegion({ reducer: ee.Reducer.sum(), geometry: region, scale: 1000, // Use 1km scale for efficiency maxPixels: 1e9 }).get('constant').getInfo(); console.log(`Plume pixels detected: ${plumeCount}`); // 4. Check for valid pixels if (plumeCount === 0 || plumeCount === null) { console.log(`C2`); return; } // 5. Calculate plume direction // Get mean latitude of plume pixels const plumeLat = plumeMask.multiply(ee.Image.pixelLonLat().select('latitude')) .reduceRegion({ reducer: ee.Reducer.mean(), geometry: region, scale: 1000, maxPixels: 1e9 }).get('constant').getInfo(); const ventLat = -37.52; // White Island latitude console.log(`Vent latitude: ${ventLat}`); console.log(`Mean plume latitude: ${plumeLat}`); // 6. Validation & Final Answer if (plumeLat === null || plumeLat === undefined || Math.abs(plumeLat) > 90) { console.log(`C3`); return; } // If plume mean latitude is SOUTH of vent (more negative in Southern Hemisphere) const isSouth = plumeLat < ventLat; console.log(`Plume travels south: ${isSouth}`); // Threshold: at least 0.01 degree difference (approx 1.1 km) if (isSouth && Math.abs(plumeLat - ventLat) > 0.01) { console.log(`A`); } else { console.log(`B`); } } async function initEE() { await new Promise((resolve, reject) => { ee.data.authenticateViaPrivateKey(privateKey, resolve, reject); }); await new Promise((resolve, reject) => { ee.initialize(null, null, resolve, reject); }); await runAnalysis(); } initEE(); ```
